dossier.public_summary: The signal is not consistent between odd and even transits and between different TESS sectors, with one sector showing a single transit about 20 times deeper than the others. That pattern and a hint of a second eclipse point to a false positive - likely contamination or a binary dominating the deep event - rather than a planet.

reasons.why: Strong odd/even depth difference inconsistent with a single planet period; implies a binary at twice the reported 13.6 d period (27.2 d).
reasons.value: 15.29 (diff 0.8449, ratio 6.4; odd 1241 ppm vs even 7997 ppm)

reasons.why: Depths are not consistent across transits; signal is carried by one or two deep events with one TESS sector (sector 92).
reasons.value: 2.943196107417098e-120, share_of_top_3 0.997, outliers 11386 ppm (+15.9 sigma) and 7997 ppm (+14.3 sigma) vs 569 ppm and 387 ppm

reasons.why: Depth changes by orders of magnitude between sectors/sectors, not expected for a planet; sector_depths_by_source confirms this is the dominant source of variation.

The huge difference is between pipeline products, but the per-transit depths show the QLP single transit is an outlier 15.9 sigma deep, and the SPOC depths are consistent. This points to a dominant bad/deep event rather than a steady planet; a real planet would show a consistent depth across sources.
reasons.value: differs_by_source, QLP 9127 +-322 ppm (S92) vs TESS-SPOC 569 ppm (+-227) and 387 ppm (+-246) in S70 and S82

reasons.why: Favours a non-zero secondary near 1/4 phase, only seen when the deep 9127 ppm transit is present, supporting an eclipsing binary/contamination rather than a flat-bottomed planet.
